scope: The lighthouse building at Split Rock in June 2012, including the buff octagonal tower, glass lantern, gallery, cleaning room and short connecting passage. The separately mapped fog signal house, keepers’ houses and visitor center are distinct structures.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The lighthouse tower is 54 feet tall atop a 130-foot cliff, with a third-order bivalve Fresnel lens.
The state restoration brief identifies the tapered octagonal brick and concrete shaft, metal and glass lantern, cleaning room and short passage.
The Minnesota Historical Society identifies its construction section and marks it as public domain.
The agency site inspection locates the entrance on the northeast side of the cleaning room and confirms the interior connection to the tower.
